summary: Multiple drone and missile attacks were reported across Ukraine, with significant activity in the eastern and northern regions. A double strike on a train in Zaporizhzhia resulted in no casualties, while attacks in Izium injured three civilians. Belarus imposed fuel restrictions at border gas stations to prevent smuggling to Russia. Russian officials reported Ukrainian strikes on military and civilian infrastructure, including a logistics center in Kotovsk. Protests in Russia emerged following Defense Minister Fedorov's resignation, with demonstrators calling for accountability. (Source: @kpszsu/68977, @UkraineNow/82730, @eRadarrua/101519, @tass_agency/385860, @UkraineNow/82744)
key_points: Drone and missile activity surged across Ukraine, with launches from Bryansk, Chernihiv, and Black Sea areas targeting multiple regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/69126, @kpszsu/68977, @eRadarrua/101519)
A double strike on a train in Zaporizhzhia by Russian forces caused no casualties due to rapid evacuation. (Source: @UkraineNow/82744)
Izium attack injured three civilians, including two children, from KAB strikes. (Source: @UkraineNow/82730)
Belarus restricted fuel sales at border gas stations to 20 liters per vehicle to curb smuggling to Russia. (Source: @eRadarrua/101519)
Russian protests erupted over Defense Minister Fedorov's resignation, with calls for accountability. (Source: @tass_agency/385860)
Russian forces claimed destruction of Ukrainian drones and a logistics center in Kotovsk, injuring 25. (Source: @tass_agency/385831, @tass_agency/385834)
Sumy and Chernihiv regions faced active drone threats and ground firefights, with multiple settlements under attack. (Source: @eRadarrua/101514, @kpszsu/69010)
Kherson region reported three civilian deaths and seven injuries from drone attacks in 24 hours. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31721)
Ukrainian forces targeted Russian military infrastructure in Crimea and Moscow region with over 1,800 drones in 24 hours. (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/31721, @tass_agency/385856)
Fuel smuggling from Belarus to Russia prompted logistical restrictions, risking shortages for local residents. (Source: @eRadarrua/101519)

sections.threat_assessment: Russian drone and missile campaigns intensified, targeting Kyiv, Moscow, and southern regions with over 1,800 drones in 24 hours. Belarus fuel restrictions may disrupt Russian logistics chains. Ukrainian strikes on Russian infrastructure, including a logistics center in Kotovsk, indicate sustained offensive capabilities. Ground firefights in Sumy and Chernihiv suggest ongoing positional warfare. Civilian casualties in Izium and Kherson highlight risks to non-combatants. (Source: @tass_agency/385856, @eRadarrua/101519, @tass_agency/385831, @ukr_leaks_eng/31721)
sections.regional_response: Belarus imposed fuel restrictions at border gas stations to curb smuggling to Russia, risking local shortages. Russian protests over Defense Minister Fedorov's resignation reflect internal political tensions. Ukraine's strikes on Russian infrastructure and continued drone activity suggest sustained pressure on Russian logistics. Germany's potential Tomahawk missile purchases signal escalatory posturing. Poland reported increased hate crimes against Ukrainians, complicating regional stability. (Source: @eRadarrua/101519, @tass_agency/385860, @tass_agency/385864, @UkraineNow/82737)
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian drone campaigns show increased sophistication, targeting both military and civilian infrastructure. Belarus fuel restrictions may strain Russian supply lines. Ukrainian strikes on Russian logistics centers indicate effective targeting. Protests in Russia over military leadership suggest potential internal vulnerabilities. Cognitive technologies courses funded by Fedorov highlight ongoing information warfare efforts. (Source: @tass_agency/385856, @eRadarrua/101519, @tass_agency/385831, @DeepStateUA/23659)
